narrative_purpose: Shows enrichment and star formation as one event: the expanding shell both scatters new elements into the surrounding gas and compresses that gas into collapsing again.
subject: An expanding roughly spherical shell of luminous debris on the left, its leading edge ragged and broken into fingers, ploughing rightward into a large dark dense cloud. Where the shell meets the cloud, the cloud edge is visibly compressed into a bright rim with two or three small dense knots already forming inside it. Behind the shell's trailing edge, thin scattered flecks of matter drift in the emptied space.
camera: Wide side-on view so the collision front reads clearly as a boundary running vertically down the middle of the frame.
scene: Interstellar space. The left half is thin, emptied, faintly lit; the right half is thick dark cloud with layered veils of haze receding into it.
light: The shell is the light source, throwing cool cyan and teal light onto the compressed cloud rim; the knots inside the rim glow faintly warm from within; the cloud interior on the far right stays almost entirely dark.
palette: Void-indigo cloud, cool cyan and teal shell light, mist-grey compressed rim, two or three small scarce amber knots, faint metallic flecks in the emptied space.
style: Painterly atmospheric astronomical plate, volumetric haze, soft dissolving edges.
detail_level: Moderate on the collision front where the compression and the forming knots must be legible; low and hazy elsewhere.
composition: Shell occupying the left third, collision front running vertically just left of centre, dark cloud filling the right two-thirds with open dark space in the lower right for a callout.
consistency_notes: No arrows or motion streaks - the direction of travel must be conveyed by the ragged leading edge and the compressed rim alone.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no motion lines, no grid, no diagram chrome, no planets, no spacecraft, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
